Prevention: Clean material, boots, clothing and farm machinery when moving out of infested areas
Seeds are spread by animals - do not allow livestock into an affected area to avoid spread
Species is spread by water - avoid runoff from surrounding infested fields
The species is spread by wind - limit seed set in surrounding populations
Avoid propagating it as hedge rows as the plant establishes itself quickly to form dense stands.
Plant khocho and gliricidia sepium instead
Monitoring: Annual or perennial herbaceous broadleaved shrub, woody at the base [2–3 (–5) m high].
Leaves greyish-green, finely hairy on underside giving a grey appearance.
Simple, 3–5 (–7) pointed lobes (6–33 cm long and 5–22cm wide).
Flowers bright yellow, daisy or sunflower-like (up to 10 cm across), carried on long and swollen stalks (7–30 cm long)
Regularly check edges of dambos and in cultivated fields for presence of the weed as it is seen and consider direct control when present
Check for flowering and seed development to prevent seed set, spread and build up of seed bank
Direct Control: Dig up or hand pull plants prior to onset of flowering, ensuring the taproot is severed well below the crown to prevent regrowth
Do not slash the plants as this will encourage sprouting
Uproot, dry and burn all plant parts to avoid re- establishment or spread
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
SC) is a post- emergence herbicide applied once the weed has germinated and before maize is sown.
Use at a rate of 23 ml in a 15 litre tank
